entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pietro Lippomano (1550-1544) was a Roman Catholic prelate who played a pivotal role in the Counter-Reformation efforts in 16th-century Italy.

As Bishop of Verona (1544–1548), he implemented various reforms aimed at strengthening the Catholic Church's presence in the region.

During his tenure as Bishop of Bergamo (1516–1544), Lippomano oversaw the construction of several new churches and the renovation of existing ones, contributing to the city's architectural and cultural heritage.

His legacy extends beyond his ecclesiastical duties, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the city's economy, fostering a period of relative peace and prosperity in Bergamo.

"The glory of God is the greatest glory," Lippomano once said, "and it is in our duty to promote it, not only in our own lives but also in the lives of those around us."

Lippomano's efforts to promote Catholicism and support the arts had a lasting impact on the cultural and religious landscape of 16th-century Italy.
